goal: Expose AO token transfer through the ArConnect-compatible injected provider surface, so a connected dApp can request an AO send via window.arweaveWallet through the same connection-approval/signing-approval flow every other provider method already uses -- resolves debt declared on AO-TOKEN-SEND-PROVIDER-BRIDGE.
outcome: PROVIDER_SURFACE_METHODS (packages/messaging/src/page-protocol.ts) gains a new AO-token-transfer method alongside connect/sign/dispatch/signDataItem/batchSignDataItem/encrypt/decrypt. A dApp calling it triggers the same approval-window flow every signing method already goes through (ApprovalHandler, never a trusted-RPC shortcut). SigningApprovalPreview (packages/core/src/models/approval.ts) gains a token/denomination field so the approval window can show the user which token and how much is being sent, instead of only a pre-formatted opaque amount/fee string. The popup-internal SendView.tsx flow (estimateTransfer/submitTransfer) is unchanged and continues to work exactly as it does today -- this adds a second, dApp-facing entry point onto the same underlying AO transfer capability ao-token-send already built, it does not replace or refactor the existing popup-internal path.

requirements.statement: The new provider-surface method is added to PROVIDER_SURFACE_METHODS in packages/messaging/src/page-protocol.ts, following the same request/response envelope shape every existing provider method already uses -- no bespoke wire shape.

Every dApp-initiated AO transfer request routes through ApprovalHandler and shows a real approval window before signing -- never a silent or auto-approved signature, matching the existing privilege-tier boundary (PROVIDER_METHODS/APPROVAL_METHODS/KEY_METHODS) enforced at the background dispatcher's single choke point.

SigningApprovalPreview (packages/core/src/models/approval.ts) gains an explicit token/denomination field. Amount/fee stay atomic-integer strings in the token's own smallest unit (AO-TOKEN-SEND-RULE-2, unchanged) -- the new field identifies which token and denomination those atomic strings are in, it does not change how amounts themselves are represented.

Signing for a provider-initiated AO transfer reuses the same key-session.ts in-memory unlocked-session cache and the same core/src/ao transfer module ao-token-send already built -- no new signing path, no password re-derivation, no duplicate AO-messaging client wiring.

The existing popup-internal SendView.tsx flow (estimateTransfer/submitTransfer called directly) is left functionally unchanged -- this task adds a second entry point, it does not migrate or remove the first.

A connected dApp can call the new provider method with a token processId, recipient, and amount, and receive a signed/submitted AO transfer result after the user approves it in the approval window -- exercised by an integration-style test through the messaging/provider-bridge path, not just a unit test of the handler in isolation.

The approval window's rendered preview for this new method shows the token identity and a correctly denominated amount, sourced from the new SigningApprovalPreview.token field -- not a generic 'sign this data' preview.

pnpm vitest run provider bridge approval connected-apps content/index background/index send receive passes; pnpm tsc -p packages/messaging --noEmit and pnpm tsc -p packages/core --noEmit pass; pnpm wxt build succeeds.
